title: Regional blue/green deployment + progressive traffic-shift safeguards for hosted API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Harden the hosted API deployment pipeline to support safe blue/green and regional rollouts with automated progressive traffic shifting and deterministic rollout gates. This ticket covers the end-to-end plan: versioning policy for deployed runtime/images, LTS channel handling, tooling for traffic-shift orchestration, observability gating, and rollback automation.

Background: The hosted API currently supports a simple canary for single-region deploys but lacks a standardized approach for multi-region blue/green swaps and progressive traffic shifts (e.g., 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%). Recent customer incidents (latency spikes during a cross-region deploy) and the need to ship runtime-2.4 features to select customers require a safer deployment path that minimizes blast radius and gives platform engineers clear, auditable gates.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: pipeline automation (GitHub Actions + deployer service), rollout policy primitives (phases, wait windows, metric gates), metric thresholds and dashboards, integration with traffic manager (edge LB / service mesh), regional sequencing, automatic rollback hooks, and an audit trail for regulatory customers.
- Out of scope: model serving format changes (handled in separate model-onboarding work) and on-prem upgrade tooling for Private (separate ticket).

Design decisions:
1) Versioning: adopt a runtime semantic tag scheme with three channels: stable-LTS (major.minor-lts-YYYYMM), stable (major.minor.patch), canary (commit-hash). Customers on Dedicated or Private can pin to an LTS tag. Hosted API default will be stable channel with controlled opt-in to canary for early access customers.
2) Blue/Green model per region: deploy green environment alongside blue (current), warm caches, run internal traffic smoke tests, then perform traffic shift using progressive percentages. Green becomes new blue after 100% success.
3) Traffic-shift orchestration: expose primitives in deploy pipeline: phases with duration, target percentage, success gates. Implement stateful driver service (deployer) that calls traffic API on the edge LB and updates routing via service mesh.
4) Gating metrics and thresholds: primary gates are error rate (5xx), p50/p95 latency, request success rate, and CPU/GPU saturation. Default thresholds: 5xx increase <0.5% absolute over baseline, p95 latency delta <20%, CPU <85% for sustained 3m. Any gate breach triggers stop+rollback.
5) Observability: require a 'rollout dashboard' with real-time charts, synthetic smoke test results, and side-by-side region comparisons. Integrate with PagerDuty for P0/P1 alerts.
6) Audit & approvals: enable manual gate override only with a two-person approval, recorded in the deployment audit trail.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Infra tasks: edge LB API support for fractional traffic, service mesh route-weighting API, DNS TTL considerations for regional failover.
- Pipeline changes: GitHub Actions workflow that orchestrates deployment phases, calls deployer service endpoints, and writes audit events.
- Deployer service: implement new endpoints /start-rollout, /advance-phase, /abort-rollout, /get-status; add idempotency keys and retries.
- Monitoring: create Canary Analyzer (config-driven) that polls Prometheus (or remote metric store) and evaluates gate expressions.
- Runbook: update runbook for hosted API rollouts with quick rollback commands and runbook escalation steps.

Success criteria:
- New pipeline performs a successful blue/green regional rollout in staging and prod-beta region without manual intervention (except optional approvals).
- Rollback path executed automatically for at least two simulated gate breaches in test harness.
- Deployment audit trail includes timestamps, user ids, gate evaluations, and traffic percentages.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: backend cache warmup causes temporary latency spikes post-swap. Mitigation: include a warmup phase with synthetic reads and slow-in ramp for cache-sensitive routes.
- Risk: traffic manager API rate limits block fast shifts. Mitigation: implement exponential backoff and split shifts across smaller increments if API throttled.
